papers.title: Flat-band-induced integer doping and phase transition in monolayer graphene
papers.authors: Z. Wang, C. Moulsdale, X. Guo, J. Liu, Z. Qiu, I. Soltero, Z. Jiang, M. Holwill, J. Wu, H. Sun, Z. Chai, A. J. H. Jones, M. Zhu, J. Yin, C. P. Y. Wong, T. Taniguchi, K. Watanabe, K. E. J. Goh, S. V. Morozov, A. Mishchenko, S. Ulstrup, L. Lin, A. H. MacDonald, G. Yu, M. I. Katsnelson, J. Lu, V. I. Fal’ko, A. K. Geim, P. Huang, C. R. Woods, K. S. Novoselov
papers.abstract: Abstract van der Waals heterostructures are stabilized by a delicate balance between van der Waals, elastic and Coulomb energies 1–4 . Because the interfaces are not covalently bonded, the constituent crystals can slide, rotate and reconstruct, resulting in several possible competing structural phases 2,5,6 . However, controlled tuning of this balance, and hence dynamical control over the stacking, has yet to be achieved. Here we report a dynamical heterostructure in which monolayer graphene is doubly aligned to bulk hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) and monolayer hexagonal boron nitride (mhBN) on either side. In such a system, a global structural phase transition, manifested as a change of crystalline symmetry observed by scanning tunnelling microscopy, could be induced by gating, magnetic field or temperature. This structural transition is accompanied by an exotic electronic transition: the doping of graphene switches between discrete levels, corresponding to an exact integer number of electrons or holes per moiré plaquette. We attribute this integer doping to charge trapping in localized, strain-induced pseudo-Landau levels (flat bands in reciprocal space 7–12 ), produced by moiré reconstruction (strongly enhanced by the mhBN). Electrical control of coupled structural and electronic phase transitions provides a route to engineering strain-induced flat bands and strain–Coulomb correlations in van der Waals heterostructures.
papers.summary_en: The authors demonstrate a gate-, field- and temperature-tunable structural phase transition in doubly aligned graphene/hBN heterostructures, accompanied by discrete changes in graphene’s carrier density. They attribute the integer doping to charge trapped in reconstruction-induced, strain-related pseudo-Landau flat bands.

papers.title: Fully Nonequilibrium Hall Response from Berry Curvature
papers.authors: Shouvik Sur, Lei Chen, Yiming Wang, Chandan Setty, Silke Paschen, Qimiao Si
papers.abstract: In topological materials, Berry curvature leads to intrinsic Hall responses. Focusing on time-reversal symmetric systems with broken inversion symmetry, a spontaneoous (zero magnetic field) Hall effect is expected to develop under an applied electric field. Motivated by recent developments in Weyl-Kondo semimetals, here we advance a fully nonequilibrium (FNE) Hall response due to the Berry curvature. In particular, we show that, while the spontaneous Hall current is quadratic in the previously described regime of weak electric field, due to the contribution from the dipole moment of the Berry curvature, the FNE Hall response for non-perturbative electric fields is not controlled by the Berry curvature dipole. Remarkably, the FNE Hall response resembles what happens in systems that break the microscopic time-reversal symmetry. We illustrate the universality of these results by comparing them with their counterparts in systems with any higher-multipole of the Berry curvature. The implications of our results for the understanding of strongly correlated topological semimetals are discussed.
papers.summary_en: This paper analyzes fully nonequilibrium Hall responses in time-reversal-symmetric, inversion-broken systems and finds that at non-perturbative electric fields the response is not governed by the Berry-curvature dipole.

papers.title: Peierls Transition and Magnetism in a Dirac Semimetal: CaMnBi 2
papers.authors: Aashish Sapkota, Niraj Aryal, Xiao Hu, Masaaki Matsuda, Yan Wu, Guangyong Xu, John M. Wilde, Andreas Kreyssig, Paul C. Canfield, Cedomir Petrovic, John M. Tranquada, Igor A. Zaliznyak
papers.abstract: Dirac semimetals of the form A Mn X 2 ( A = alkaline-earth or divalent rare earth; X = Bi , Sb) host conducting square-net Dirac-electron layers of X atoms interleaved with antiferromagnetic Mn X layers. Hypervalent pnictogen square nets have long been predicted to host an electronically driven Peierls instability, whereas low-temperature anomalies in CaMnBi 2 near T * ∼ 50 K have previously been discussed in terms of possible magnetic canting, time-reversal symmetry breaking, and a resulting Weyl-semimetal state. Here we use polarized and unpolarized neutron diffraction, x-ray diffraction, and density functional theory to investigate this transition in single-crystal CaMnBi 2 . We observe a structural symmetry-lowering transition at T * = 46 ( 2 ) K from a tetragonal lattice with C -type antiferromagnetism to an orthorhombic phase with unit-cell doubling along the c axis, minimal impact on magnetism, and no measurable uniform spin canting ( ≲ 2 ° ). Superlattice peak intensities and the lattice distortion reveal a continuous second-order transition governed by a single primary order parameter. The refined displacement pattern corresponds to a zigzag bond-order-wave (BOW) modulation of in-plane Bi–Bi bonds, providing direct diffraction evidence for a Peierls-type instability of the Dirac-electron Bi layer anticipated by Hoffmann and co-workers [; ]. These results identify the T * anomaly as an intrinsic Dirac-electron-driven Peierls-BOW transition of the Bi square net.
papers.summary_en: The study identifies the approximately 46 K anomaly in CaMnBi₂ as a continuous structural transition to an orthorhombic phase with a zigzag Bi–Bi bond-order-wave modulation, rather than a transition driven by substantial magnetic canting. The authors interpret this as a Peierls-type instability of the Dirac-electron Bi square net.

The reported small magnetic response also makes it useful to distinguish structural and magnetic contributions in future studies of the transition.
papers.future_zh: 后续研究可进一步阐明已识别的键序波相变如何影响Bi方格网的电子性质，以及它与材料低温异常之间的关系。由于该转变伴随的磁性变化很小，未来研究也可据此区分相变中的结构与磁性贡献。

papers.title: Designing dislocation-driven polar vortex networks in twisted perovskites
papers.authors: W. Sandholt, N. Gauquelin, J. Mangeri, A. Annys, J. M. Hansen, A. R. Insinga, E. Dollekamp, N. Vitaliti, G. Panchal, T. Chennit, A. De Backer, D. Kepaptsoglou, R. Mandal, D. R. Rodrigues, S. Van Aert, H. Nguyen, K. I. Wurster, A. Bhowmik, I. E. Castelli, S. B. Simonsen, T. S. Jespersen, Q. M. Ramasse, R. D. James, B. Jalan, J. Verbeeck, J. M. G. Lastra, N. Pryds
papers.abstract: Twisting two atomic layers produces a geometric moiré pattern but bonding-induced interfacial reconstruction fundamentally transforms this into an ordered dislocation network—a distinction obscured in weakly bonded van der Waals systems. Although in-plane topological vortex nanostructures arising from twisting-induced lateral strain modulation have been linked to periodic moiré patterns in freestanding perovskite layers1–3 and 2D bilayers4, their coupling to the interfacial dislocation network in twisted layers remains unresolved. Here we demonstrate that twisted freestanding SrTiO3 (STO) layers undergo interfacial reconstruction into a network of screw dislocations, accompanied by the emergence of in-plane topological vortices. Unlike in previous reports, these vortices are associated with the dislocation network rather than with geometric moiré patterns. Four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4DSTEM) reveals a beam deflection texture in registry with the interfacial dislocation network. A machine learning interatomic potential, trained on first-principles calculations, together with phase-field modelling, confirms that competing strains within the dislocation network stabilize polar vortex–antivortex pairs; first-principles calculations further reveal the emergence of an electronic superlattice with a well-defined periodicity. Our results establish twist-controlled dislocation networks as a new and versatile route to designing local polar and electronic structures in oxide materials. Experimental and theoretical investigation of twisted freestanding SrTiO3 layers using various analytic methods from 4DSTEM to DFT reveal a long-range ordered screw dislocation pattern as well as topological polar vortex arrays in the interface plane.

papers.title: Evidence for p-wave magnetism in electronic band structure of metallic EuSi
papers.authors: Erjian Cheng, Yixing Yang, Yifan Gao, Jan Priessnitz, Yiqing Hao, Jieyi Liu, Rui Lou, Alexander Fedorov, Mengyu Yao, Yuri Prots, Houke Chen, Ralf Koban, Xuemin Shi, Ying-Ting Chan, Ulrich Burkhardt, Berit H. Goodge, Walter Schnelle, Vicky Hasse, Jaafar Ansari, Zhuocheng Lu, Peter Bencok, Gerrit van der Laan, Makoto Hashimoto, Donghui Lu, Jacek Osiecki, Zhanfeng Liu, Shengtao Cui, Jaime Sánchez-Barriga, Oliver Rader, Yulin Chen, Hua Wang, Jiadong Zang, Leila Noohinejad, Weida Wu, Libor Šmejkal, Junwei Liu, Zhongkai Liu, Claudia Felser
papers.abstract: Abstract One active frontier of quantum-matter research is the realization of p -wave symmetry-breaking phases in fermionic systems, long exemplified by the A phase of superfluid helium-3 (refs. 1–3 ). Achieving p -wave superconductivity 4 and its magnetic analogue 5 —characterized by a time-reversal-symmetric, p -wave spin-polarized Fermi surface—remains a grand challenge 6,7 . Despite recent progress in identifying candidate p -wave magnets 5,7–10 , spin-resolved spectroscopic evidence for their electronic structures remains limited. Here we report angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and spin-ARPES evidence for p -wave magnetism in the near-Fermi-level electronic structure of stoichiometric metallic EuSi, supported by symmetry analysis, first-principles calculations and neutron scattering. Neutron diffraction reveals a chiral spiral phase between 33.4 K and 62 K that fulfils archetypal p -wave magnetism criteria: it preserves the combined symmetry of time reversal and lattice translation, while breaking inversion symmetry. Spin-integrated ARPES reveals a pronounced magnetism-driven reconstruction of the electronic structure, with energy separations exceeding 100 meV, and spin-ARPES resolves S y polarization in near-Fermi-level spectral features. The extracted S y exhibits a sign-changing modulation across successive magnetic Brillouin zones and is suppressed near the nodal regions, consistent with the predicted p -wave spin texture and unfolded spin-polarization calculations. Magnetic force microscopy and micro-ARPES further reveal approximately 10-μm chiral magnetic domains. These results identify EuSi as a stoichiometric metallic platform for investigating p -wave magnetism in electronic band structures and spin-symmetry-based functionalities in spintronics 10 , topological matter 7 , superconductivity 11 and beyond.
papers.summary_en: The authors present spectroscopic evidence for p-wave magnetism in stoichiometric metallic EuSi, combining spin-resolved electronic-structure measurements with symmetry analysis, calculations and neutron scattering. The measured spin polarization and magnetic-zone dependence are consistent with the predicted p-wave spin texture.

papers.abstract: We construct a two-dimensional 2-band tight-binding model with two-body interactions and without magnetic lattice translation, in which both the hopping and interaction are exponentially local (with Gaussian decay) in real space. The interaction is built from pair annihilation operators whose coefficients are hopping amplitudes divided by positive powers of relative distance. Without any band projection, the ground states at $1/3$ filling are exactly fractional Chern insulator (FCI) states (and thus have nonzero gap) for any finite lattice size with any periodic/twist boundary conditions. Although their potential as spin qubits, quantum sensors and single-photon emitters has been demonstrated experimentally, creating them deterministically and identifying them chemically remains challenging, which limits control over their electronic states. papers.abstract: What makes a topological character prominent is whether its characteristic electronic states are located near the Fermi energy. While the kagome-metals possess unique topological characteristics owing to their distinctive electronic band structures, i.e. flat and Dirac bands, the control of Fermi energy to accentuate these characteristics has scarcely been studied in these materials. Here, we propose a new concept for activating the topological characteristics of Weyl electrons specifically near the interface of kagome-bilayers, namely interface Weyl electrons. The kagome-bilayers prepared by a sputtering technique surprisingly exhibit atomically abrupt interfaces thanks to the suppression of interdiffusion for maintaining the crystal symmetry of the hexagonal-type D0$_{19}$ and cubic-type L1$_{2}$ structures. Much higher electrical conductivity of the kagome-bilayers compared to single-layer films indicates the emergent contribution of a highly conductive electronic state at the interfaces. The enhanced electrical conductivity and the exceptionally large anomalous Hall conductivity about 2000 $Ω$$^{-1}$cm$^{-1}$ in the intrinsic mechanism indicates that the emergent interface electronic states comprise Weyl nodes in the D0$_{19}$ structure identified in our theoretical band calculations, triggered by nontrivial charge transfer. These results demonstrate that topological transport can be engineered at the interface of intermetallic compounds, leading further design principles towards development of device functionality.

papers.abstract: Noncrystallographic rotational symmetry offers a route to unconventional spin splitting beyond the constraints of periodic crystals. We show that circularly polarized light induces odd-parity $h$-wave magnetism in a collinear antiferromagnetic Penrose quasicrystal without spin-orbit coupling. Light-induced chiral hopping, generated by virtual two-step processes, combines with staggered exchange to lift the spin degeneracy of the undriven system. Quasicrystalline spin-group symmetry enforces odd-parity spin splitting and selects $h$-wave as its leading angular harmonic. An analytical effective quasi-band theory relates this splitting to the geometry of local hopping paths and predicts its reversal upon switching the light helicity. Momentum-resolved spectral calculations reveal the characteristic alternating spin contrast, for which we propose spin-resolved time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy as an experimental probe. Our results establish a mechanism for optically controlling higher-harmonic odd-parity magnetism and demonstrate how quasicrystalline order extends Floquet engineering beyond crystallographic symmetry constraints.

papers.abstract: The emergent properties of strongly correlated materials can be highly sensitive to how they are made, yet synthesis pathway is rarely treated as a fundamental variable governing their ground states. The spinel ZnV$_2$O$_4$ provides a model system in which to test this idea: its pyrochlore lattice of antiferromagnetically coupled V$^{3+}$ $S=1$ moments hosts competing spin and orbital degeneracies, while different synthesis routes yield markedly different low-temperature behaviour. Here, we show that changing the solid-state synthesis pathway reproducibly selects a distinct structural and magnetic ground state. Microwave-assisted solid-state synthesis (MASS) stabilises the cubic spinel structure to low temperature, suppressing the conventional cubic-to-tetragonal transition and preserving the highly frustrated $S=1$ pyrochlore lattice. Combining high-resolution diffraction, magnetometry and inelastic neutron scattering, we find a magnetic ground state exhibiting persistent spin-liquid-like dynamics together with partial spin freezing. Our results establish synthesis pathway as an experimental variable for selecting between competing emergent states in strongly correlated materials, revealing a route to accessing ground states not realised by conventional synthesis.

papers.abstract: Orbital magnetization is a fundamental measure of time-reversal symmetry breaking in solids that is accessible by experiments. However, unlike the well-studied equilibrium case, the understanding of orbital magnetism resulting from external stimuli such as light and electric fields is still in its infancy. Here we employ a novel real-space framework to investigate charge-to-orbital conversion in a metallic orbital antiferromagnet beyond the conventional Bloch-band picture. We find that common point defects give rise to strongly enhanced time-odd magnetoelectric effects and, depending on their local symmetry, further activate otherwise-forbidden time-even responses. Moreover, we introduce a local marker that provides spatially resolved information on the orbital magnetization carried by non-equilibrium states. Real-space maps reveal that point defects create nanoscale hotspots of orbital magnetization leading to a profound modification of the bulk magnetoelectric response, including a sign reversal of the net orbital moment. Our findings may open up the possibility of engineering linear-response orbital moments with atomic-scale precision by point defects and impurities.

papers.abstract: Spatial inversion forbids the conventional electric-dipole second-order bulk charge and spin photovoltaic responses in centrosymmetric crystals. Here we show that a phase-coherent two-color field at frequencies $ω$ and $2ω$ can generate symmetry-selected charge and spin photocurrents through an inversion-even third-order dc response. A systematic symmetry analysis of centrosymmetric magnetic point groups and collinear antiferromagnetic spin point groups shows that pure-spin channels are allowed in a broad class of such systems under appropriate two-color driving. papers.abstract: Layered ferromagnets with strongly correlated electrons provide a platform for exploring the interplay among magnetism, spin-orbit coupling, and nontrivial band topology. $\mathrm{Ni}_{1/4}\mathrm{TaSe}_2$ is a correlated van der Waals ferromagnet with a transition temperature of 58 K that lies close in composition to a superconducting phase that emerges upon Ni depletion. papers.abstract: Coherent control of fermions has become a standard approach for engineering quantum devices. Here, we explore parity-induced frustration in multiterminal Josephson arrays. We focus on odd-parity Josephson trijunctions, where the presence of a trapped fermion induces a phase winding in each trijunction. Connecting these trijunctions constrains their shared phases, resulting in a long-distance phase coherence where the frustrated configurations dominate the low-energy physics. In the classical regime, these arrays map onto the Kagome XY antiferromagnet, whose established Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) transition yields algebraically decaying $6e$ phase correlations. We show that the $6e$ phase coherence is manifested as a pronounced third harmonic in the current-phase relation of these arrays. While quantum phase fluctuations suppress the $6e$ coherence, we show that through spin-orbit coupling they also lead to spin correlations and entanglement between the trapped fermions. Our results establish fermion-induced frustration as a route to composite superconducting coherence and phase-mediated spin entanglement in superconductor-semiconductor artificial quantum materials.

papers.abstract: We investigate the collective excitations of isolated and crystalline $\mathbb{CP}^{2}$ skyrmions in a two-dimensional triangular-lattice spin-1 magnet. Within an $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ coherent-state framework, fluctuations of the magnetic dipole and quadrupole moments are described by two coupled bosonic flavors. In a uniform spin-polarized state, these flavors can be identified with single-spin-flip and double-spin-flip excitations, whereas a nonuniform $\mathbb{CP}^{2}$ texture mixes their character. We formulate the corresponding bosonic Bogoliubov--de Gennes problem and examine the matrix-valued gauge connection governing flavor-wave propagation. For isolated skyrmions, the calculated spectrum contains localized modes, and the scattering dynamics exhibit transverse deflection accompanied by isospin precession. For a numerically relaxed skyrmion crystal, we obtain collective-mode bands with nonzero Chern numbers and calculate the associated thermal Hall response. These findings illustrate how projective magnetic textures couple multipolar excitations to non-Abelian transport and topological band phenomena.

papers.abstract: Germanium (Ge) hosts four degenerate valleys in the conduction band minima, and their highly anisotropic effective masses offer a valley degree of freedom in transport phenomena via anisotropic conductivity. Using time- and polarization-resolved terahertz spectroscopy combined with deformation potential theory, we reveal a valley relaxation time reaching 10 ps near the band edge of Ge(001) at room temperature, long enough to detect the valley polarization in electrical transport measurements. papers.summary_zh: 该研究利用太赫兹光谱发现，Ge(001) 在室温下、接近带边处的谷弛豫时间最长可达 10 ps，并展示了用非共振光脉冲在亚皮秒内完全反转谷极化。结果指向在块体锗中实现谷极化的电学探测与超快调控。
papers.method_en: The authors combine time- and polarization-resolved terahertz spectroscopy with deformation-potential theory to study valley relaxation in Ge(001). They use off-resonant light pulses to demonstrate optical control of the valley polarization.
papers.method_zh: 作者结合时间分辨、偏振分辨太赫兹光谱与形变势理论，研究 Ge(001) 中的谷弛豫。研究还使用非共振光脉冲展示对谷极化的光学调控。
papers.result_en: Near the band edge at room temperature, the measured valley relaxation time reaches 10 ps, which the authors identify as long enough for electrical-transport detection. Off-resonant pulses reverse the valley polarization completely in less than a picosecond, with the abstract describing the energy consumption as extremely low but giving no numerical value.
papers.result_zh: 在室温带边附近，测得的谷弛豫时间可达 10 ps；作者认为这一时间足以支持电输运探测。非共振光脉冲可在亚皮秒内完全反转谷极化；摘要称其能耗极低，但未给出具体数值。
papers.future_en: The results motivate room-temperature valleytronics based on bulk indirect-gap semiconductors compatible with existing electronics.
papers.future_zh: 这些结果为利用可兼容现有电子技术的块体间接带隙半导体发展室温谷电子学提供了依据。
papers.tier_reason_en: The abstract reports a distinctive room-temperature relaxation timescale together with sub-picosecond, complete optical reversal, making the combined measurement and control result broadly significant beyond a narrowly specialized materials study.
papers.tier_reason_zh: 摘要报告了具有代表性的室温弛豫时间，以及亚皮秒完全光学反转谷极化的结果；这种测量与调控的结合具有超出单一材料专题研究的广泛意义。
